title: Strict finite quotient representatives for coefficient extension
statement: For a prime l, finite extensions E,L of Q_l, an embedding iota:E→L, a scheme W, a derived reduction calculus SE and compatible scalar-system data A, let C be reduction by SE followed by derived scalar extension by A. Given the balanced ordinary association at every quotient, there is a functor direct on flat-term K-flat complexes over the completed E-coefficients, with values in complexes of actual L-coefficient systems. Its nth evaluation is naturally the specified ordinary tensor complex with A_L,n, and its successor transitions are the specified quotient tensor maps on all local sections. There is a natural isomorphism C(QP) ≅ Q(direct P) whose nth evaluation equals the composite of SE reduction evaluation, its K-flat finite comparison, A levelwise K-flat comparison, and the given tensor association. For every derived K over the completed E-coefficients, C(K) is a normalized L-coefficient sequence: each transition is universal for scalar restriction from level n to any higher level. Uses [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] and [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

source.place: Integral operations and normalized coefficient reduction model.

proof.text: Apply the ordinary strict tensor existence theorem to obtain direct, its finite evaluation isomorphisms, and the specified actual quotient transitions. The ordinary construction is isolated from all derived comparisons.

Apply the strict derived comparison to this ordinary model, the given scalar-system data, reduction calculus, and balanced association. It supplies the natural model isomorphism with its exact finite evaluation equation.

For each good representative, the strict tensor normalization theorem supplies normalization of Q(direct P). To reach an arbitrary derived K, take a flat-term K-flat resolution of a representative of K. Transport its exact tensor-right flatness through siteSheafTensorRightIso to obtain a good P and an isomorphism Q(P) to K. Transport normalization first along model(P) inverse and then along coefficientExtensionSystem applied to that resolution isomorphism. Normalization is invariant under system isomorphism: naturality of the actual derived transitions conjugates its Hom map by the two finite evaluation isomorphisms, preserving injectivity and surjectivity.

proof_origin.place: Proof steps 1--3 decomposed; K-flat representative and normalization-isomorphism transport proved in Lean

lean.statement:
theorem coefficientExtensionStrictRepresentative_exists
    (SE : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E W)
    (association : ∀ n : ℕ,
      scalarReductionExtension l E W n ⋙ (A.levels n).model.E ≅
        integralScalarReduction l E L ι W n)
    (hassociation : IsCoefficientExtensionAssociation l E L ι W A association) :
    ∃ (direct : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E W).FullSubcategory ⥤
        CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l L W) ℤ)
      (directEvaluation : ∀ n : ℕ,
        direct ⋙ (coefficientSequenceEvaluation l L W n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ≅
          (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E W).ι ⋙ integralScalarFiniteComplex l E L ι W n)
      (model : integralOperationsGoodLocalization l E W ⋙
        coefficientExtensionSystem l E L ι W SE A ≅ direct ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q),
      IsCoefficientExtensionStrictTransition l E L ι W direct directEvaluation ∧
      IsCoefficientExtensionModelEvaluation l E L ι W SE A association direct
        directEvaluation model ∧
      ∀ K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E W),
        IsNormalizedCoefficientSequence l L W
          ((coefficientExtensionSystem l E L ι W SE A).obj K)
